revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Making Moves
revealWordProblem.text: A group of friends are planning to make a movie. They research the running times of movies made. The data they collected are shown in the histogram. They have asked for your advice on how long their movie should run. What do you recommend? Explain your recommendation based on the data presented in the histogram.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Add up the histogram's frequencies: 7 + 30 + 39 + 22 + 12 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 114 movies total. The tallest bar is the 101–115 minute interval with 39 movies, the mode of the data. Combined with the neighboring 86–100 minute interval (30 movies), that's 30 + 39 = 69 of the 114 movies, or 69 ÷ 114 ≈ 0.605 = 60.5%, running between 86 and 115 minutes. Very few movies run longer than 145 minutes (2 + 1 + 1 = 4 movies, about 3.5%). Based on this data, I'd recommend the friends aim for a running time in the 101–115 minute range, since that's the most common length and keeps their movie in line with most movies made.

onLevel.stem: A histogram of test scores shows: 50–59: 2, 60–69: 5, 70–79: 10, 80–89: 8, 90–99: 3. Which interval has the most students?
onLevel.explanation: The 70–79 interval has the highest frequency of 10 students.
choiceFeedback: That interval holds the highest scores, but the question asks where the most students are. Compare the frequencies, not the score ranges.
5 is less than 10—which bar is tallest?
Compare: 2, 5, 10, 8, 3—the largest is 10.
hints: 'Most students' means the highest frequency — compare the counts 2, 5, 10, 8, 3, not the score ranges themselves.
Careful: the highest scores (90–99) don't mean the most students. Find the largest of the five frequencies first, then read off its interval.
First step: circle the largest number among 2, 5, 10, 8, 3. Then match that count back to its interval — and check the choice pairs both parts.
onLevel.stemEs: Un histograma de calificaciones muestra: 50–59: 2, 60–69: 5, 70–79: 10, 80–89: 8, 90–99: 3. ¿Qué intervalo tiene la mayor cantidad de estudiantes?
onLevel.explanationEs: El intervalo 70–79 tiene la frecuencia más alta, con 10 estudiantes.

onLevel.stem: A histogram of goals-per-game shows: 0–1: 9 players, 2–3: 6, 4–5: 3, 6–7: 1. What shape is this distribution?
choices: Skewed right (most players low, tail toward high values)
Skewed left (most players high, tail toward low values)
onLevel.explanation: The tallest bars are at the low end (0–1) and the bars shrink as goals increase — the tail points right, so it is skewed right.
choiceFeedback: A symmetric shape would have the bars mirroring each other around the center. Compare the 9 at the low end with the 1 at the high end.
Are the bars roughly equal height? This isn't symmetric.
Most are low (left), tail goes high (right)—that's right skew.
hints: Sketch the bars: heights 9, 6, 3, 1 from left to right. Notice which side is tall and which way the heights trail off.
Skew is named for the TAIL — the long, low side — not for the peak. Find the direction the bars shrink toward, then name that direction.
First step: the tallest bar (9 players) is at 0–1 goals on the left, and heights fall to 1 by 6–7. Trace the tail with your finger, then name it.
onLevel.stemEs: Un histograma de goles por partido muestra: 0–1: 9 jugadores, 2–3: 6, 4–5: 3, 6–7: 1. ¿Qué forma tiene esta distribución?
onLevel.explanationEs: Las barras más altas están en el extremo bajo (0–1) y se van encogiendo a medida que aumentan los goles: la cola apunta a la derecha, así que está sesgada a la derecha.

onLevel.title: Spot the Interval Mistake

workedExample.label: Conclusion
workedExample.work: The student drew three bars and said the histogram was complete.

onLevel.correctWork: The intervals are not equal in width and they leave a gap. 0–5 and 6–10 each cover 6 values, but 12–18 covers 7 values and the value 11 has no bin at all. Histogram intervals must be equal-width and cover every value with no gaps. Using equal intervals of 5 (0–4, 5–9, 10–14, 15–19) gives frequencies 0–4: 2 (the 1 and 4), 5–9: 2 (the 6 and 9), 10–14: 1 (the 12), and 15–19: 2 (the 15 and 18), totaling 7.
hints: Check the width of each interval the student used. Are 0–5, 6–10, and 12–18 all the same size?
Where would a value of 11 go? Every value needs exactly one equal-width bin — there can be no gaps.
onLevel.explanation: The problem starts at the interval-choosing step: 0–5 and 6–10 are 6 wide, 12–18 is 7 wide, and the value 11 has nowhere to go. Equal-width bins of 5 fix both problems — 0–4: 2, 5–9: 2, 10–14: 1, 15–19: 2, totaling all 7 assist values.
onLevel.explanationEs: El problema empieza en el paso de elegir intervalos: 0–5 y 6–10 miden 6, 12–18 mide 7, y el valor 11 no tiene dónde ir. Casillas del mismo ancho de 5 arreglan las dos cosas: 0–4: 2, 5–9: 2, 10–14: 1, 15–19: 2, lo que cubre los 7 valores de asistencias.

onLevel.title: Find the Histogram Error

workedExample.label: Conclusion
workedExample.work: The histogram is symmetric because the bars go 1, 2, 3, 4, 2.

onLevel.correctWork: The frequencies are correct (1, 2, 3, 4, 2), but this is NOT symmetric. In a symmetric histogram, the bars rise and fall evenly from the center. Here the bars increase from left to right and only drop at the end — the data is skewed LEFT (most scores are on the higher end).
hints: Symmetric means the left side mirrors the right side. Does 1, 2, 3, 4, 2 mirror evenly?
The peak (4) is in the 80–89 range, which is toward the right. That means most data is on the high end.
onLevel.explanation: The frequency table is right; the Conclusion step is what fails. Symmetric means the left half mirrors the right half, but 1, 2, 3, 4, 2 climbs steadily and peaks at 80–89 near the right end, so the data is skewed left with most scores on the high side.
onLevel.explanationEs: La tabla de frecuencias está bien; lo que falla es el paso de la Conclusión. Simétrico significa que la mitad izquierda refleja la derecha, pero 1, 2, 3, 4, 2 sube de manera constante y llega a su punto máximo en 80–89, cerca del extremo derecho, así que los datos están sesgados a la izquierda con la mayoría de las calificaciones en el lado alto.

extending.prompt: A teacher collected test scores and made two different histograms — one with intervals of 5 (50–54, 55–59, etc.) and one with intervals of 20 (50–69, 70–89, 90–109). Both use the same data. How might the two histograms look different? Which interval size gives you more detail about the distribution? When might the larger interval be better?
extending.sentenceFrame: The histogram with intervals of 5 would have ___ bars and show ___. The histogram with intervals of 20 would have ___ bars and show ___. Smaller intervals are better when ___, and larger intervals are better when ___.
extending.hint: Count how many values fall into each interval for both histograms—look at bar heights.
hints: Same data, two bucket sizes. Think: chopping scores into many small buckets vs a few big buckets — what changes about the picture?
Compare three things: how many bars each histogram has, how tall its bars get, and how clearly you can see the shape, peaks, or gaps.
Start with a count: intervals of 5 covering 50–109 make 12 bars; intervals of 20 make just 3. Write what 12 skinny bars reveal that 3 wide ones hide.
extending.explanation: Intervals of 5 across 50–109 make 12 narrow bars with small frequencies, so peaks, gaps, and the exact shape show up clearly. Intervals of 20 make only 3 tall bars that smooth those details away, which is useful when the data set is large or you only want the big-picture comparison of low, middle, and high scores.
extending.explanationEs: Intervalos de 5 a lo largo de 50–109 forman 12 barras angostas con frecuencias pequeñas, así que los picos, los huecos y la forma exacta se ven con claridad. Intervalos de 20 forman solo 3 barras altas que borran esos detalles, lo cual sirve cuando el conjunto de datos es grande o solo quieres la comparación general entre calificaciones bajas, medias y altas.

extending.stem: A histogram of points-per-game has its tallest bars on the LEFT (low scores) and a long tail stretching RIGHT toward a few high scorers. How is this distribution described?
extending.explanation: The tail points right (toward the high values), so it is skewed right — most players are clustered at the low end.
choiceFeedback: It is tempting to name a skew after where the tall bars sit. A skew is named for the direction the long tail stretches instead.
Left skew has the tail on the left, not right.
Symmetric means roughly equal—this has a clear tail.
hints: Underline the two location words in the stem: tallest bars on the LEFT, long tail stretching RIGHT. Skew is named after one of those.
Rule: a distribution is skewed in the direction its TAIL stretches, not where its peak sits. Decide which way the tail points here.
First step: the stem says the tail stretches toward the few high scorers. Apply the tail rule to name the skew — don't follow the peak.
extending.stemEs: Un histograma de puntos por partido tiene sus barras más altas a la IZQUIERDA (puntajes bajos) y una cola larga que se extiende hacia la DERECHA, hacia unos pocos anotadores altos. ¿Cómo se describe esta distribución?
extending.explanationEs: La cola apunta a la derecha (hacia los valores altos), así que está sesgada a la derecha: la mayoría de los jugadores se agrupa en el extremo bajo.

extending.stem: Two histograms show the SAME 40 test scores — one uses intervals of 5, the other intervals of 20. Which statement is true?
choices: The interval-of-5 histogram leaves some scores out
The interval-of-5 histogram has more bars and shows more detail about the shape
The interval-of-20 histogram has more bars
Both histograms must look exactly the same
extending.explanation: Smaller intervals create more bars and reveal finer detail; larger intervals smooth the shape into fewer bars. Both still include all 40 scores.
choiceFeedback: Changing the interval width regroups the data but never throws any of it away — all 40 scores still land in some bar.
Wider intervals gather more values into each bar, so they produce fewer bars. Think about how many 20-wide bins it takes to cover the same range.
Smaller intervals show more detail—more bars, finer shape.
hints: Both histograms use all 40 scores — the only difference is bucket width: 5 points vs 20 points per interval.
Reason it out: covering the same score range with narrower buckets requires MORE buckets. Then ask what having more bars does for detail.
First step: take the range 60–79. With width 20 it's ONE bar; with width 5 it becomes four bars (60–64, 65–69, 70–74, 75–79). Compare the detail.
extending.stemEs: Dos histogramas muestran los MISMOS 40 puntajes: uno usa intervalos de 5 y el otro intervalos de 20. ¿Qué afirmación es verdadera?
extending.explanationEs: Los intervalos más pequeños crean más barras y revelan detalles más finos; los intervalos más grandes suavizan la forma en menos barras. Ambos histogramas siguen incluyendo los 40 puntajes.

extending.stem: Data: 4, 8, 9, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 22, 24, 27, 31, 33. How many values fall in the 10–19 interval?
extending.explanation: The values 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, and 19 all fall between 10 and 19, so the frequency for that bin is 6.
choiceFeedback: That count sweeps in values from outside the interval. Only numbers from 10 through 19 belong in this bin.
Did you count correctly which values fall in 10–19?
Not all values fit in that interval—count carefully.
extending.stemEs: Datos: 4, 8, 9, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 22, 24, 27, 31, 33. ¿Cuántos valores caen en el intervalo 10–19?
extending.explanationEs: Los valores 12, 14, 15, 17, 18 y 19 caen entre 10 y 19, así que la frecuencia de ese intervalo es 6.
hints: A frequency is just a count of how many values land inside one interval, endpoints included.
Go through the list in order and mark only the numbers that are at least 10 and no more than 19.
The first value in that range is 12, and 9 is too small to count. Keep working down the list and tally the ones that qualify.
hintsEs: Una frecuencia es simplemente el conteo de cuántos valores caen dentro de un intervalo, incluyendo los extremos.
Recorre la lista en orden y marca solo los números que sean al menos 10 y no más de 19.
El primer valor en ese rango es 12, y el 9 es demasiado pequeño para contar. Sigue bajando por la lista y cuenta los que califican.

extending.stem: Frequencies: 0–9: 3, 10–19: 9, 20–29: 5, 30–39: 2. Which interval has the tallest bar?
extending.explanation: The 10–19 interval has the greatest frequency (9 players), so its bar is the tallest.
choiceFeedback: That interval sits in the middle of the range, but height depends on the count. Compare the frequencies 3, 9, 5, and 2 directly.
The tallest bar shows the highest frequency—which interval is it?
Compare 3, 9, 5, 2—which number is biggest?
extending.stemEs: Frecuencias: 0–9: 3, 10–19: 9, 20–29: 5, 30–39: 2. ¿Qué intervalo tiene la barra más alta?
extending.explanationEs: El intervalo 10–19 tiene la mayor frecuencia (9 jugadores), así que su barra es la más alta.
hints: Bar height comes from the frequency, not from how large the numbers in the interval are.
List the four frequencies on their own and compare them as plain numbers.
The counts are 3, 9, 5, and 2. Decide which of those is greatest and read off the interval it belongs to.
hintsEs: La altura de una barra viene de la frecuencia, no de qué tan grandes son los números del intervalo.
Escribe las cuatro frecuencias por separado y compáralas como números simples.
Los conteos son 3, 9, 5 y 2. Decide cuál es el mayor y lee el intervalo al que pertenece.

extending.stem: Read this histogram of assists per game — 0–4: 2 players, 5–9: 8 players, 10–14: 5 players, 15–19: 1 player. About how many players are on the team?
extending.explanation: Add every bar's frequency: 2 + 8 + 5 + 1 = 16 players total.
choiceFeedback: That sum leaves one of the bars out. Every interval contributes, so add all four frequencies: 2, 8, 5, and 1.
Check which interval holds the most readings.
Histogram shows frequency by interval, not individual values.
extending.stemEs: Lee este histograma de asistencias por partido: 0–4: 2 jugadores, 5–9: 8 jugadores, 10–14: 5 jugadores, 15–19: 1 jugador. ¿Aproximadamente cuántos jugadores hay en el equipo?
extending.explanationEs: Suma la frecuencia de cada barra: 2 + 8 + 5 + 1 = 16 jugadores en total.
hints: Every player in the data set is counted in exactly one bar, so no one is left out and no one is doubled.
Find the team size by adding the frequencies of all the bars together.
Start with 2 + 8 = 10, then keep adding the remaining two frequencies.
hintsEs: Cada jugador del conjunto de datos se cuenta en exactamente una barra, así que nadie queda fuera ni se cuenta dos veces.
Halla el tamaño del equipo sumando las frecuencias de todas las barras.
Comienza con 2 + 8 = 10 y luego sigue sumando las otras dos frecuencias.

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — The Boundary Mistake

workedExample.label: Conclusion
workedExample.work: Total = 3 + 4 + 2 = 9 values, so the histogram shows 9 players.

extending.correctWork: There are only 7 data values, but the count adds up to 9. The mistake is that the boundary value 10 was counted twice — once in 0–9 and again in 10–19. Each value belongs to exactly ONE bin. The value 10 fits only in 10–19, and 20 fits only in 20–29. The correct counts are 0–9: 2 (the 5 and 9), 10–19: 3 (the 10, 14, and 19), and 20–29: 2 (the 20 and 22), which totals 7.
hints: Count the data values first: 5, 9, 10, 14, 19, 20, 22 is 7 values, but the frequencies add to 9. A value got counted twice.
A boundary value like 10 belongs to only one interval. Since 10–19 starts at 10, the value 10 goes there, not in 0–9.
extending.titleEs: Extensión Nivel 2 — El error de la frontera
extending.explanation: There are 7 data values but the frequency count adds to 9, so something was counted twice. The boundary value 10 was placed in both 0–9 and 10–19; since 10–19 starts at 10, that value belongs there only, making the correct counts 0–9: 2, 10–19: 3, and 20–29: 2, for a total of 7.
extending.explanationEs: Hay 7 valores de datos, pero el conteo de frecuencias suma 9, así que algo se contó dos veces. El valor frontera 10 se colocó tanto en 0–9 como en 10–19; como 10–19 empieza en 10, ese valor va solo ahí, y los conteos correctos quedan 0–9: 2, 10–19: 3 y 20–29: 2, para un total de 7.

extending.stem: A histogram shows these frequencies: 0–4: 3 players, 5–9: 8 players, 10–14: 12 players, 15–19: 5 players. How many players are represented in total?
choiceFeedback: That total leaves out part of the data. Every bar contributes, so add all four frequencies together — including the shortest bar.
Did you count frequencies or find the highest value?
Add all frequencies: 3+8+12+5.
hints: The question asks for the TOTAL across all four intervals — not the tallest bar and not the biggest interval.
Each frequency counts the players in one interval, and no player is counted twice — so combine all four frequencies into one total.
Set up the addition: 3 + 8 + 12 + 5. The sum of all the bar heights is the total number of players.
extending.stemEs: Un histograma muestra estas frecuencias: 0–4: 3 jugadores, 5–9: 8 jugadores, 10–14: 12 jugadores, 15–19: 5 jugadores. ¿Cuántos jugadores se representan en total?

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Display Data: Histograms is counting a boundary value in two intervals at once — for example, putting the value 10 in both the '0–9' bin and the '10–19' bin. Each data value belongs to exactly ONE interval. Before you submit, add up all your frequencies and check that the total matches the number of data values you started with.

check.stem: Which interval has the most players?

check.stem: How many players take between 3 and 8 shots per game?
check.explanation: 8 players in the 3–5 bar plus 10 players in the 6–8 bar = 18 of the 23 players.

check.stem: Does the histogram support the coach's claim?
choices: Yes — 18 of 23 players cluster in the middle intervals
No — the data is skewed right

questions.stem: On a box plot, what does the line inside the box represent?
questions.explanation: The line inside the box of a box plot always represents the median.
